objective: Propose a HYPERBOLIC quality metric for an exported Stage-2 Semantic-ID table that correlates with the Stage-3 test Recall@10 of the run that read it. The metric is a NUMBER computed from the SID table; nothing is trained, no Stage 2 and no Stage 3 run is made, and the metric must be computable in under a minute on 24587 items. It must be judged on 97 SID+recall pairs that already exist.
contract:
A METRIC is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. HYPERBOLIC CONSTRUCTION: the number uses an explicit curved operation -- a Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, a geodesic or Frechet barycentre in a ball of fixed negative curvature, a tangent-space comparison that is only meaningful because of the map. A Euclidean distance in disguise does not qualify, and the proposal must say where the curvature enters.
  2. COMPUTABLE FROM THE TABLE: the inputs are the exported SID table (the integer code per item and level), optionally the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference (source/target representations per item, learned on training pairs only) and optionally the TRAINING split. Nothing else.
  3. NO LEAKAGE: no validation interaction and no test interaction may enter the number, directly or through a fitted quantity. A metric that reads the recall, the Stage 3 run, or a validation/test pair is out of scope.
  4. FIXED FORM: no free parameter tuned against the 97 recalls. Any constant must be derived (from the codebook size, the item count, the reference's own temperature) and stated.
  5. ONE NUMBER: the metric returns one scalar per SID table, higher meaning better. Diagnostics that need a second number to interpret are out of scope.
A metric that simply re-expresses the prefix count, the collision rate or the same-bucket ratio is out of scope: those are already measured and the bucket count does not track recall (Spearman -0.065 on the 97 pairs).

metrics.title: Hyperbolic history-barycentre enrichment of the true level-1 SID prefix over a size-matched null.
metrics.formula:
Symbols: N = number of items; c = c_ref = fixed negative curvature of the frozen reference (c = 1 if the reference reports unit curvature); d_c(x,y) = geodesic distance in the Poincare ball B^d_c; t_j = target-side reference representation of item j in B^d_c; s_u = source-side representation of u; c1(j) = level-1 integer SID code of item j; n_k = #{j : c1(j) = k}; tau = tau_ref (the reference's training temperature).
For each source u in the TRAINING split let H(u) = {j : (u,j) is a training pair}. For each i in H(u) with |H(u)| >= 2 put H(u,i) = H(u) \ {i} and
  b(u,i) = argmin_{b in B^d_c} sum_{j in H(u,i)} d_c(b, t_j)^2,
computed by the Karcher iteration b <- exp_b( (1/|H(u,i)|) sum_{j in H(u,i)} log_b(t_j) ), started from the Euclidean mean of {t_j} projected into the ball, stopped at ||log_b(new)|| < 1e-6 or 50 iterations.
For every item j define
  q_j(u,i) = exp(-d_c(b(u,i), t_j)/tau) / sum_{l=1}^{N} exp(-d_c(b(u,i), t_l)/tau).
Let k+(u,i) = c1(i) and Q_{k+}(u,i) = sum_{j : c1(j) = k+(u,i)} q_j(u,i). Then
  lift(u,i) = log( Q_{k+}(u,i) * N / n_{k+(u,i)} )
and
  METRIC = (1/|U|) sum_{u in U} (1/|H(u)|) sum_{i in H(u)} lift(u,i),
where U = {u : |H(u)| >= 2}. Higher is better. If tau_ref is not exposed, tau = median_{(u,i)} d_c(b(u,i), t_i) / log N (derived, not tuned). If H(u,i) is empty the example is skipped.
metrics.inputs: (i) the exported SID table, only the level-1 integer code c1(j) for each of the N items; (ii) the frozen Issue #126 reference, only its target-side representations t_j for all items, its fixed curvature c_ref and its training temperature tau_ref; (iii) the TRAINING split, only the pairs (u,j). No validation interaction, no test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 output.
metrics.geometry: The construction lives in the Poincare ball B^d_c of fixed negative curvature -c. The query point b(u,i) is a Frechet/Karcher barycentre computed with the ball's exp and log maps, and every distance is the geodesic distance d_c(x,y) = (1/sqrt(c)) arcosh(1 + 2c||x-y||^2 / ((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2))). Curvature enters twice: in the barycentre, which is the hyperbolic least-squares centre of the history and not a Euclidean mean, and in every distance inside the temperatured softmax. A Euclidean distance in the same coordinates is not isometric to the ball and would change both the barycentre and the softmax ranking, so the curvature is not a cosmetic rescaling.
metrics.why: Stage-3 retrieves with the level-1 prefix as the coarse address. If the prefix partition is aligned with the reference geometry, the true target's prefix is the region of the ball where the user's history mass actually sits. The metric is the log-density of that region: the positive cell's total temperatured softmax mass Q_{k+} divided by the mass n_{k+}/N it would carry if the codes were independent of geometry. It adds over Q_H: (1) the query point is the Frechet barycentre of the whole training history, not one source anchor, so it uses the full context and is robust to a noisy last item; (2) the positive is scored against the full item-level negative distribution (all N items, temperatured), not the mean of ten negatives, so the shape of the negative cloud matters; (3) the size-matched null n_{k+}/N removes the collapse reward that made plain path likelihood anti-correlate with recall; (4) unlike a hard bucket-reach count there is no radius and no hard reachability, the full softmax mass is used and the query is a barycentre. Q_H sees a small-sample ranking from a single anchor; this sees whether the coarse prefix is the geometrically enriched region for the entire history against the entire item population.
metrics.compute: The reference part is table-independent and is computed once for all 97 tables: each Karcher barycentre costs O(|H(u,i)|*d) per iteration (<= 50 iterations) and each softmax row costs O(N*d); with N = 24587, d <= 64 and P = O(N) examples this is a few 10^10 flops, chunked over examples in float32, seconds to tens of seconds. For each SID table only c1 changes: n_k is one O(N) pass and Q_{k+}(u,i) is the sum of the precomputed q over the items of cell k+, which is O(|cell k+|) per example, or a single scatter-add O(N) per table plus O(1) per example; K <= 256. Total per table is far below a minute; precompute q once and never recompute it per table.
metrics.risks: (1) If tau_ref is very small the softmax saturates on the nearest item, Q_{k+} approaches q_{i+}, and the metric degenerates to a single-anchor nearest-neighbour score; if tau_ref is very large the softmax is uniform and lift is near 0 for every table. tau is fixed by the reference, not tuned. (2) Leave-one-out histories of length 1 are skipped, so if most sources have one interaction P shrinks and the estimate is noisy. (3) Sources whose history is geometrically spread have an unstable Karcher mean near the boundary; cap the Karcher step at 0.5 and project into the ball (numerical safeguard, not a tuned parameter). (4) Random tables sit slightly below 0 by Jensen; compare only tables with the same N and comparable K, which the 97 pairs satisfy. (5) If the training split is unrepresentative of validation/test sources the lift may not transfer. (6) The metric reads only level 1 and cannot see recall gained from a good level-2+ code while level 1 is meaningless.
metrics.failure_mode: Worst on a table whose level-1 codes are assigned by a random hash of the item id, or by clustering on the source side or on a modality unrelated to the target geometry: the true target's cell then carries no enrichment over its size, so lift is near 0 and can go negative if the hash is anti-aligned. A fully collapsed one-cell table is also at 0 (Q = 1, n/N = 1), so collapse is not rewarded. The metric is also worst, by construction, on a table that gets its Stage-3 recall entirely from level-2+ codes while its level-1 prefix is geometrically meaningless, because the formula deliberately reads only level 1.

metrics.title: Hyperbolic history-barycentre expected-rank lift of the true level-1 SID cell over a size-matched random relabelling.
metrics.formula: Items a = 1..N (N = 24587). SID table gives a level-1 digit pi(a) in {0..255}; deeper levels are not read. TRAIN is a set E of ordered pairs (i,j) (query item i, target item j). For each query i let H_i = { j' : (i,j') in E } and let E' = { (i,j) in E : |H_i| >= 2 }. The frozen reference supplies, for every item a, a source vector s_a in R^d, a target vector t_a in R^d, and a temperature tau > 0. Curvature is c = 1. Define exp_0(u) = tanh(||u||/2) * u/||u|| (exp_0(0)=0), r(v) = min( tanh(||v||/(2*tau)), 1 - 1/N ), emb(v) = r(v) * v/||v||, p_a = emb(s_a), q_a = emb(t_a). Mobius addition at c=1: x (+) y = ( (1 + 2<x,y> + ||y||^2) x + (1 - ||x||^2) y ) / ( 1 + 2<x,y> + ||x||^2 ||y||^2 ). Poincare distance: d_H(x,y) = 2 * artanh( ||(-x) (+) y|| ). Riemannian log and exp: log_x(y) = d_H(x,y) * ((-x) (+) y)/||(-x) (+) y|| (0 if x = y); exp_x(v) = x (+) ( tanh(||v||/2) * v/||v|| ), exp_x(0) = x. Frechet (Karcher) barycentre B(S) of a finite set S with uniform weights: b_0 = exp_0( (1/|S|) * sum_{y in S} log_0(y) ); b_{r+1} = exp_{b_r}( (1/|S|) * sum_{y in S} log_{b_r}(y) ), for r = 0..19 (20 iterations, fixed). Cell prototypes: for every level-1 digit k with C_k = { a : pi(a) = k } nonempty, m_k = B({ q_a : a in C_k }); n_1 = number of nonempty level-1 cells. History point for a pair (i,j) in E': h_ij = B({ q_{j'} : j' in H_i, j' != j }). Distances: delta_ij(k) = d_H(h_ij, m_k). Temperature: T = median over (i,j) in E' of delta_ij(pi(j)); if that median is 0, T = 1. Expected rank: rho_ij = sum_{k != pi(j)} sigma( ( delta_ij(pi(j)) - delta_ij(k) ) / T ), with sigma(z) = 1/(1 + e^{-z}). Metric: HBRL = (1/|E'|) * sum_{(i,j) in E'} ln( (n_1 + 1) / ( 2 * (rho_ij + 1) ) ). Conventions: HBRL = 0 if n_1 < 2 or E' is empty. Higher is better; 0 is the value of a partition independent of the reference; the maximum is ln((n_1+1)/2).
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table (integer code per item per level; only the level-1 digit is read); the frozen Issue #126 reference's per-item source vectors, per-item target vectors and temperature tau; the TRAIN split's (query item, target item) pairs. Nothing else: no validation interaction, no test interaction, no recall, no Stage 2 or Stage 3 run.
metrics.geometry: unit Poincare ball with curvature c = 1, i.e. constant sectional curvature -1. Curvature enters at four explicit points: (i) the data are pushed into the ball by the exponential map exp_0(v/tau), so the radius of every point is the hyperbolic function tanh(||v||/(2 tau)) and not a linear rescaling; (ii) every distance is the Poincare distance built from Mobius addition and 2*artanh, whose argument is not a Euclidean norm; (iii) both barycentre families (the cell prototypes m_k and the history points h_ij) are Frechet/Karcher minimisers of the sum of squared hyperbolic distances, computed with the exp/log fixed-point iteration, and are not arithmetic means; (iv) T is expressed in the same curvature units. Taking c -> 0 removes the artanh and the Mobius correction, makes the barycentres arithmetic means, and changes the number, so this is not a Euclidean distance in disguise.
metrics.why: Stage-3 recall needs the true target's level-1 token to be among the first tokens the decoder emits for a query, and a table is learnable exactly when that token is a low-entropy function of what the model conditions on. The Karcher barycentre of the query's whole remaining history is the minimum-variance hyperbolic summary of that conditioning set, and it lives on the target channel, which Q_H never uses. The score is not a two-way margin: it is the expected number of the n_1 cell prototypes that the geometry ranks ahead of the correct cell, so rho_ij < 9 means the correct level-1 cell typically sits inside a top-10 cell list, the prefix-level analogue of Recall@10. The null is exact and size-matched: because sigma(z) + sigma(-z) = 1, the expected soft rank of a uniformly random cell under the same distances is exactly rho_0 = (n_1 - 1)/2, so the log-lift cancels the pure size effect and a 2-code table caps at ln 1.5 = 0.405 while a 256-cell table reaches ln 128.5 = 4.856; a collapsed trie therefore cannot win, which is what sank likelihood-style scores. The metric is invariant to relabelling the level-1 digits, since a permutation of the digits permutes the m_k identically, so it scores the partition and not the code values. Over Q_H it adds three things: the query point pools the entire training history instead of one anchor, the contrast is the full level-1 catalogue instead of a mean over ten sampled negatives, and the value is an expected rank rather than a margin, so its scale is a count of competitors.
metrics.compute: O(N*d) for the embeddings; 256 Karcher means over the whole catalogue (N point-visits, 20 iterations); one Karcher mean per evaluated pair over its leave-one-out history, O( sum_i |H_i|^2 * 20 * d ); then |E'| * n_1 Poincare distances, O(|E'| * n_1 * d). At 24587 items, 256 codes, d <= 64 and roughly 2.5e5 training pairs this is about 1e10 flops, a few seconds to about 20 s in vectorised NumPy/BLAS, processed in query blocks of 1024; no N x N matrix and no N x n_1 matrix is ever held, so memory stays under 1 GB.
metrics.risks: the construction needs the reference's source and target heads to live in one shared metric space, which its contrastive training provides but which must be true or d_H(h_ij, m_k) is meaningless. In a small-tau regime the embedding saturates at the radius cap, all distances grow, T grows with them and rho_ij is compressed toward rho_0 for every table, which loses variance across the 97 tables. Pairs are unweighted, so queries with very long histories contribute many highly stable barycentres and can dominate the mean. Deeper levels are ignored by design, so tables that differ only below level 1 are indistinguishable. If the 97 tables mostly share a level-1 partition the metric has no variance to correlate with. The fixed 20-step Karcher iteration can drift toward the boundary for near-antipodal history sets, and the leave-one-out history point degenerates when the remaining history is a single item.
metrics.failure_mode: it must be worst on the table whose level-1 digit is an independent hash of the item index: then pi(j) is exchangeable with every other cell relative to h_ij, rho_ij converges to (n_1 - 1)/2 and HBRL converges to 0 no matter what the reference says. The two degenerate ends are also bad by construction: n_1 = 1 returns 0, and the 2-code, 3-code and 12-code collapsed tables are capped at 0.405, 0.693 and 1.870 respectively, all below a healthy 256-cell table at rho = 5, which scores 3.07. In the other direction it is deliberately blind: a table with a perfect level-1 and a random level-2 scores exactly as high as one with a good level-2, which is the price of not reading the near-identifier prefixes.

metrics.title: Hyperbolic leave-one-out mass-rank percentile of the true level-1 SID cell.
metrics.formula: Let N be the number of items that have both a level-1 integer code and a target representation, K the number of distinct level-1 codes, c_i in {1,...,K} the code of item i, n_p = #{i : c_i = p}, and P_train the set of training interaction pairs. Work in the unit Poincare ball B^d = {x in R^d : ||x|| < 1} with constant curvature -1 and d_H(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2||x-y||^2 / ((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))). For a finite set Z = {z_1,...,z_m} in B^d, let Bary(Z) be the Frechet/Karcher barycentre argmin_{z in B^d} sum_i d_H(z,z_i)^2, computed in the Lorentz model by 20 iterations of z <- exp_z(mean_i log_z(z_i)), initialised at the normalised Lorentzian sum, stopping when the step norm is below 1e-6; Bary(empty) = 0 (the ball origin). For each training pair (u,j) in P_train let H_u = {k : (u,k) in P_train} and define the query point q_{u,j} = Bary({s_u} union {t_k : k in H_u, k != j}), where s_u is the frozen source representation of u and t_k the frozen target representation of k. For each code p let b_p = Bary({t_i : c_i = p}) for p != c_j, and b_{c_j}^{-j} = Bary({t_i : c_i = c_j, i != j}); put d_p = d_H(q_{u,j}, b_p), with b_{c_j} replaced by b_{c_j}^{-j}, and d_true = d_{c_j}. Then P_{u,j} = (1/N) [ sum_{p : d_p < d_true} n_p + 0.5 n_{c_j} + 0.5 sum_{p != c_j : d_p = d_true} n_p ]. Finally M = 0.5 - (1/|U|) sum_{u in U} (1/|H_u|) sum_{j in H_u} P_{u,j}, where U is the set of queries with at least one training pair. Higher M is better.
metrics.inputs: the exported SID table's level-1 integer code per item (all levels may be present, but only level 1 is read); the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference arrays s_i and t_i for every item, learned on training pairs only; and the training split P_train. Nothing else: no validation interaction, no test interaction, no recall, no Stage-3 artifact.
metrics.geometry: the unit Poincare ball of curvature -1. Every distance is d_H, every cell summary and every query-history summary is a Frechet/Karcher barycentre in that ball, the leave-one-out true-cell barycentre and the empty-set origin are hyperbolic conventions, and the curvature enters both in the denominator (1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2) of d_H and in the exp/log maps of the barycentre iteration. A Euclidean replacement of either the distance or the barycentre is a different metric and is not this one. If the frozen reference stores coordinates in a ball of curvature -c_ref, first rescale every coordinate by sqrt(c_ref) to the unit ball; this is an isometry and does not change the curvature sign.
metrics.why: Stage-3 Recall@10 is high when the level-1 prefix of a target is the prefix selected by the query's reference geometry and that prefix is fine enough to resolve the target. P_{u,j} is the fraction of item mass that the table ranks ahead of the true cell, with the true cell's own mass counted at half; it is small only when the true cell is near the query-history barycentre and its own mass is small. A fine aligned table therefore gives P near 0 and M near +0.5; a random table gives P near 0.5 and M near 0; a collapsed table gives P near 0.5 and M near 0 because the true cell's own mass dominates its percentile; an anti-aligned table gives P near 1 and M near -0.5. This adds over Q_H in three ways: the query point is the Frechet barycentre of the whole leave-one-out training history plus the source point, not a single source anchor; the contrast is the full mass distribution over all K level-1 cells, not a mean over ten negatives; and the 0.5 symmetry baseline is exact for a percentile, so the metric cannot reward a table merely for collapsing into one large cell. It is a mass percentile, not a likelihood, margin, tightness or coverage.
metrics.compute: cell barycentres cost O(20 d N); query barycentres cost O(20 d sum_u |H_u|^2); the distance and rank step costs O(|P_train| K d). At N = 24587, K <= 256, d <= 64 and 250k training pairs with mean history 10, this is roughly 7 GFLOP; float32 vectorised Lorentz Karcher and NumPy distance blocks finish in well under a minute. There is no Stage-2 run, no Stage-3 run, no fitting, no permutation null and no free parameter.
metrics.risks: (1) if s_i and t_i are not in a common unit ball, the barycentres are not meaningful; the reference must document a shared ball or an exp map into it. (2) Very long histories make the leave-one-out query barycentre cost quadratic in |H_u|; a 1M-pair split with 50 interactions per query can approach the minute, although typical splits do not. (3) If target representations cluster near the origin, many distances tie, P tends to 0.5 and M tends to 0, so the metric loses discrimination. (4) The 0.5 centring assumes exchangeability of codes with respect to the reference geometry; if the table was itself built from the reference, the baseline is conservative rather than invalid. (5) Poincare distances overflow near the boundary; use Lorentz coordinates and clamp ||x|| <= 1 - 1e-7. (6) Only level 1 is read; if a particular Stage-3 run is driven by level-2/3 prefixes, this metric will miss that component.
metrics.failure_mode: the table on which it must be worst is the level-1 assignment anti-aligned with the reference: a fixed permutation that sends, for every training query, the reference-nearest items into the cell farthest from the query-history barycentre, with small cells. Then the true cell is last, P_{u,j} tends to 1 and M tends to -0.5. A random balanced table gives M near 0. A single-code table (K = 1) has all distances tied and M = 0 by convention, so collapse is neutral rather than rewarded; a giant-cell-plus-singletons table also gives M near 0 because the true cell's own mass dominates its percentile.

metrics.title: Resolution-matched hyperbolic Gibbs-mass enrichment of each item's own SID cell, with the item excluded from its own neighbourhood.
metrics.formula: Let N be the number of exported items, L the number of levels, c_l(j) the integer code of item j at level l, and B_l(j) = {j' : c_1..l(j') = c_1..l(j)} its level-l prefix cell. Let K_l = the number of distinct level-l prefixes. Fix K = 10 (the Recall@10 cut) and set l* = max{ l in 1..L : K_l <= N/K }; if no level satisfies this, l* = 1. The frozen reference supplies source vectors s_u and target vectors t_j in the open Poincare ball D^d of curvature -1, plus its own softmax temperature tau > 0. For every item i with at least one training positive, let P_i be the set of training users who interacted with i, and define q_i = argmin_{q in D^d} sum_{u in P_i} d_H(q, s_u)^2, the hyperbolic Karcher/Frechet barycentre, computed by the Poincare exp/log fixed-point iteration. Here d_H(q,t) = arcosh(1 + 2||q-t||^2 / ((1-||q||^2)(1-||t||^2))) is the Poincare distance; the iteration uses Moebius addition and exp_q/log_q with curvature -1. Put w_i(j) = exp(-d_H(q_i, t_j)/tau) for j != i. Let C_i = B_l*(i) minus {i} and c_i = |C_i|. If c_i = 0 set E_i = 0; otherwise set W_i = sum_{j in C_i} w_i(j), Z_i = sum_{j != i} w_i(j), and E_i = ln( W_i / ( (c_i/(N-1)) * Z_i ) ). The metric is M = (1/|A|) sum_{i in A} E_i, where A is the set of items with at least one training positive. M is one scalar; larger is better.
metrics.inputs: (1) the exported SID table: one integer code per item per level; (2) the frozen Issue #126 reference: source vector per training user, target vector per item, and its softmax temperature tau; (3) the TRAINING split positives only, used to form P_i and q_i. No validation or test interaction, no recall, and no fitted quantity is read.
metrics.geometry: All operations are in the Poincare ball of fixed curvature -1. The query point q_i is a geodesic Frechet/Karcher barycentre of the training users' source representations (Poincare exp/log and Moebius addition). Every weight w_i(j) is a negative Poincare geodesic distance d_H(q_i,t_j) passed through the reference's temperature. Curvature enters both in the barycentre (a Euclidean mean of s_u would be a different point and would change every q_i) and in every distance and weight. The size-matched null is a probability-space ratio, not a Euclidean distance.
metrics.why: For each item i the number asks whether the level of the SID tree whose codebook is matched to the Recall@10 resolution puts i together with the items the frozen reference says actually surround i's training audience. W_i/Z_i is the fraction of the reference's full temperatured negative mass that falls inside i's own cell; c_i/(N-1) is exactly the fraction a size-matched random cell would capture. Their log-ratio is a pointwise mutual information: zero for a random, collapsed or singleton cell, positive when the cell carries more of the reference's neighbourhood than its size deserves, and negative when it is anti-aligned. It adds over Q_H because Q_H uses one anchor source representation and a mean over ten negatives, whereas this uses (a) a hyperbolic barycentre of the whole training audience of the item, which averages out per-user noise and captures co-consumption, (b) the whole temperatured negative distribution through Z_i instead of a ten-negative mean, and (c) the table's own codebook size to evaluate at the level that can actually hold ten candidates, rather than at level 1 only. The explicit size-matched denominator is what the plain path likelihood lacked: it removes the collapse reward.
metrics.compute: At most N = 24587 anchors, each requiring distances to the other N-1 targets and one Karcher barycentre over its training users: about 6.0e8 Poincare distances. With precomputed squared target norms, blocked float32 arrays, and log-sum-exp normalisation this is a single pass over an N-by-N distance matrix, roughly 40-60 s on one CPU core with NumPy and less on a GPU; extra memory is O(N). The Karcher iterations are O(sum_i |P_i| d), negligible.
metrics.risks: tau must be the reference's own temperature; if tau is tiny the weights collapse to a nearest-neighbour indicator and the estimator becomes noisy, and if tau is huge all weights flatten and M tends to 0. The Poincare ball must be clipped to radius 1-1e-7. l* is 1 for most 256-code tables, so the number may be dominated by level 1; deeper levels are used only when their codebook still satisfies K_l <= N/10. Items with very few training positives have noisy audience barycentres. The null assumes a cell is a uniform random subset of the other N-1 items; a table whose cell membership correlates with reference mass in a way unrelated to retrieval could still score high.
metrics.failure_mode: Worst on an adversarial anti-aligned hash at the chosen resolution: items grouped into level-l* cells independently of their reference neighbourhoods, so W_i/((c_i/(N-1)) Z_i) is far below 1 for most anchors and M is strongly negative. The fully collapsed one-cell table scores exactly 0, and any table that becomes item-identifying at or above the chosen level also scores 0 because singletons contribute nothing; the metric therefore deliberately refuses to reward collapse or fragmentation. It under-rates a table whose only geometric splits occur below the N/K codebook budget, since l* never goes there.
